model.name: Dataset
model.purpose: Describe datasets as catalogued assets: identifiable collections of data with descriptive metadata, distributions, access services, catalogue listings, series and version relations, rights, coverage, and pointers to schema, lineage and quality, independently of storage format or access interface.
model.scope_statement: The operating surface for understanding, creating, inspecting and governing a catalogued dataset: identity and citation; classification; catalogue and harvest membership; dataset series; versioning and lifecycle status; distributions and data services; licences and access rights; temporal and spatial coverage; declared schema or profile conformance; composed lineage and quality evidence; holder, publisher and contact roles; legal, security and privacy constraints; persistence, withdrawal and erasure. Applies uniformly to open data portals, research repositories and internal registers.
in_scope: Identity and citation of the catalogued dataset
Classification by type, theme and subject
Uniform application to open data portals, research repositories and internal registers
out_of_scope: Byte-level records, tables, fields and data-contract validation rules belong in WM-DAT-004 rather than this catalogue-asset model.
Full provenance graphs, processing activities and qualified derivations belong in WM-DAT-006; this model only records dataset-level generation and derivation pointers.
Full quality metric catalogues, measurement datasets and fitness methodologies belong in WM-DAT-007; this model only attaches quality evidence to a catalogued asset.
Data products as marketable offerings, SLAs and commercial packaging belong in WM-DAT-008 (offering versus bytes).
Machine-learning training-run configuration belongs in WM-AI-006; the run references datasets.
Research-study design and protocol belong in WM-ACT-036; a study may produce datasets.
Statistical methodology, sample design and official-statistics semantics stay in an official-statistics sibling, even when a statistical release is catalogued here as a dataset.
Interactive user-interface design of a data service is outside DCAT and outside this model.
Physical samples, instruments, sensors and facilities as first-class catalogued things are DCAT extension points, not core dataset semantics.
Pricing, valuation and contractual deal terms are data-product concerns, not dataset catalogue concerns.

boundary_notes.distinction: A dataset is a conceptual collection of data published or curated by a single agent or identifiable community and available in one or more serializations or via services; a distribution is one accessible manifestation; a data service is an API that serves one or more datasets.
A catalogue is itself a dataset whose members are metadata records; a catalogue record is registration metadata about a resource, not the resource.
Dataset series group separately published datasets that share characteristics; multiple distributions of one dataset are not automatically a series.
Distributions of one dataset need not be information-equivalent.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Identifier sets of related catalogue objects
boundary_notes.distinction: Identifiers of dataset, distribution, data service, catalogue and catalogue record must remain distinct.

boundary_notes.neighbor: External standards and application profiles (DCAT, DCAT-AP, DataCite, ISO 19115)
boundary_notes.distinction: External standards are alignments. A deployment is not DCAT-, DCAT-AP-, DataCite- or ISO 19115-conformant merely because this meta-model cites those specifications.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Dataset Exchange Working Group. Core vocabulary for Dataset, Distribution, DataService, Catalog, CatalogRecord and DatasetSeries, plus version properties, checksum and coverage terms used throughout this model.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Data on the Web Best Practices Working Group. Supplies quality measurement, metric, dimension, certificate and feedback terms attached to catalogued datasets and distributions.

sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema Documentation for the Publication and Citation of Research Data and Other Research Outputs
sources.relevance: Maintained by the DataCite Metadata Working Group. Mandatory citation properties, DOI identity, alternate identifiers, date types including Withdrawn, relation types and GeoLocation.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Provenance Working Group. Generation, derivation, attribution, revision and invalidation terms reused by DCAT and by the lineage sibling model.

sources.title: DCAT-AP 3.0
sources.relevance: Published by the SEMIC action, Interoperable Europe. European application profile: mandatory properties, controlled vocabularies, catalogue-record obligations, checksum formatting and the explicit DatasetSeries rule.

sources.title: schema.org Dataset
sources.relevance: Equivalent class for dcat:Dataset; DataDownload distributions that need not contain equivalent information.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1:2014 Geographic information — Metadata — Part 1: Fundamentals
sources.relevance: Published by ISO/TC 211. Geographic metadata fundamentals: scope codes, extent, constraint and lineage packages aligned here without duplication.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1 Metadata Best Practice Guide
sources.organization: Intergovernmental Committee on Surveying and Mapping (Australia / New Zealand)
sources.version_or_date: Guidance compiled for ISO 19115-1:2014 including Amd.1:2018; page dated 2021-09-18
sources.relevance: Compiled by the ICSM Metadata Working Group. Public best-practice guidance used to align ISO 19115-1 constraint, lineage and extent practice where the ISO text is paywalled.

bundles.name: Catalogue asset
bundles.description: Identify the dataset as a catalogued conceptual collection, record citation and classification metadata, and locate it in one or more catalogues or registers.
bundles.rationale: Identity, citation, classification and catalogue membership are what make a dataset findable and citable as an asset, before any bytes are served.

layers.name: Dataset identity
layers.description: Persistent identifiers and citation-bearing descriptive metadata that name the dataset distinctly from its catalogue record and distributions.

findings.name: Persistent identifiers
findings.description: A catalogued dataset must have a persistent identity distinct from its catalogue record and from each distribution. DCAT recommends global IRIs for main classes and records dcterms:identifier on the resource. DataCite requires a DOI as the mandatory Identifier for resources registered in its system, with AlternateIdentifier for other schemes. A date is not an identifier. Master-system identifiers, governed IRIs or DOIs, and locally assigned UUIDs or ULIDs form a priority chain.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier uniquely names this dataset in the holder or repository of record, and which system assigned it?
If a DOI, catalogue IRI and local key all exist, which identifier is the citation identifier and which is the catalogue resource IRI?
Are the dataset identifier, each distribution identifier, each data-service identifier and the catalogue-record identifier pairwise distinct, and is any of them a date?

data_elements.name: master_system_identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier in the holder or repository system of record

data_elements.name: identifier_scheme
data_elements.description: Scheme code or URI such as DOI, catalogue PID or handle

data_elements.name: global_iri
data_elements.description: Dereferenceable IRI of the dcat:Dataset resource

data_elements.name: doi
data_elements.description: DataCite DOI when the dataset is registered for citation

data_elements.name: alternate_identifiers
data_elements.description: Other identifiers with types, including ISBN, accession numbers, local keys

data_elements.name: assigning_system
data_elements.description: System that minted the master identifier

artifacts.name: Persistent identifier assignment record
artifacts.description: Assignment of master-system identifier, optional DOI and alternate identifiers, with scheme and assigning system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset master-system identifier plus the assigning system, following the identity priority of master-system identifier, then governed IRI or DOI, then assigned UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Citation and descriptive metadata
findings.description: DCAT describes a dataset with dcterms:title, dcterms:description, dcat:keyword, dcterms:language, dcterms:issued, dcterms:modified and dcat:landingPage. DataCite makes Identifier, Creator, Title, Publisher, PublicationYear and ResourceType mandatory for citation. Landing pages point at the original provider, not an aggregator page. Multilingual titles and descriptions are expected in DCAT-AP.

questions.text: What is the preferred title and abstract of this dataset in each declared metadata language?
What landing page, if any, does the original data provider publish, as distinct from aggregator or catalogue pages?
Which creator, publisher, title, publication year and identifier should be used to build a DataCite-style citation, and are any mandatory values replaced by DataCite unknown-information codes?

data_elements.name: title
data_elements.description: Name given to the dataset, repeatable by language

data_elements.name: languages
data_elements.description: ISO language tags of the data and of the metadata

data_elements.name: landing_page
data_elements.description: Provider web page for human access

artifacts.name: Dataset citation and description record
artifacts.description: Titles, abstracts, keywords, languages, landing page and citation year used to discover and cite the asset.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset identifier it describes, with language tags distinguishing parallel titles and abstracts.

layers.name: Thematic classification
layers.description: Type, theme and subject classification of the catalogued resource against governed vocabularies.

findings.name: Type, theme and subject
findings.description: DCAT classifies datasets with dcterms:type from governed vocabularies such as DCMI Type, ISO 19115 MD_Scope codes or DataCite resourceTypeGeneral, and with dcat:theme concepts from a catalogue theme taxonomy. DCAT-AP requires the EU NAL data-theme vocabulary for dcat:theme when exchanging in Europe. DataCite Subject is recommended. Resource type Dataset in DataCite is not identical to a DCAT DatasetSeries or DataService.

questions.text: Is this catalogued resource a Dataset, DatasetSeries, DataService, Catalog, or another dcat:Resource subclass, and which dcterms:type or DataCite resourceTypeGeneral is declared?
Which theme concepts apply, from which concept scheme, and is the EU NAL data-theme vocabulary required for the exchange profile in force?
If ISO 19115 identification metadata is maintained, what MD_Scope code distinguishes dataset, dataset series, service or other resource kinds?

data_elements.name: resource_type
data_elements.description: dcterms:type or DataCite resourceTypeGeneral plus free-text resourceType

data_elements.name: themes
data_elements.description: SKOS concepts from the catalogue theme taxonomy

data_elements.name: subjects
data_elements.description: Subject terms with optional scheme and classification code

data_elements.name: theme_taxonomy
data_elements.description: Concept scheme used by the catalogue

data_elements.name: scope_code
data_elements.description: ISO 19115 MD_Scope code when geospatial metadata applies

artifacts.name: Dataset classification record
artifacts.description: Type, themes, subjects and taxonomy references used for discovery.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset identifier plus the concept schemes of the declared types and themes.

layers.name: Catalogue membership
layers.description: Registration of the resource in catalogues, and the catalogue and harvest structures that list it.

findings.name: Catalogue record
findings.description: A dcat:CatalogRecord describes registration of a resource in a catalogue and is optional. It carries foaf:primaryTopic to the catalogued resource, dcterms:issued as listing date and dcterms:modified as record update date. DCAT-AP makes catalogue-record modification date and primary topic mandatory when records are exchanged, and adds adms:status as change type plus optional source metadata for harvested records. The record identifier is not the dataset identifier.

questions.text: Which catalogue lists this resource, and which catalogue record has this resource as its sole primary topic?
When was the dataset issued by the holder, when was it listed in this catalogue, and when was the catalogue record last modified?
If this listing was harvested, what is the source catalogue record and what editorial change type applies to the local record?

data_elements.name: primary_topic
data_elements.description: The dataset, series or service described

data_elements.name: listing_datetime
data_elements.description: When the description was included in the catalogue

data_elements.name: record_modified_datetime
data_elements.description: When the catalogue entry last changed

data_elements.name: record_status
data_elements.description: Editorial change type of the record

artifacts.name: Catalogue record
artifacts.description: Registration metadata linking a catalogue entry to exactly one catalogued resource.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the catalogue-record IRI, which stays distinct from the identifier of its single primary-topic resource.

findings.name: Catalogue and harvest
findings.description: A dcat:Catalog is a curated collection of metadata about datasets, data services and optionally nested catalogues. DCAT-AP requires catalogue title, description and publisher, and treats empty catalogues without datasets or services as a problem signal. Aggregated DCAT metadata can serve as a preservation manifest. Harvest must preserve dataset identity and must not collapse catalogue-record identity into dataset identity.

questions.text: Which datasets, data services and child catalogues are members of this catalogue, and is the catalogue empty?
Under which application profile (DCAT 3, DCAT-AP 3.0, DCAT-US or another) is this catalogue exported, and which controlled vocabularies are mandatory in that profile?
If the same dataset is listed in several catalogues, which listing is the holder catalogue of record versus a harvested copy?

artifacts.name: Catalogue harvest feed
artifacts.description: Profile-shaped serialization of catalogue, records and catalogued resources for aggregation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the catalogue IRI plus the declared application profile and the harvest observation time.

bundles.name: Distribution and access
bundles.description: Describe how the conceptual dataset is made available as files or services, how bytes can be authenticated, and under which licence and access-rights rules.
bundles.rationale: Serving bytes, authenticating them and gating them are separable from identifying and describing the asset, and they bind to distributions and services rather than to the dataset alone.

layers.name: Distribution
layers.description: Accessible manifestations of the dataset, their URLs and formats, and the integrity and packaging of downloadable bytes.

findings.name: Accessible representation
findings.description: A dcat:Distribution is an accessible form of a dataset such as a downloadable file. DCAT distinguishes dcat:downloadURL (direct file) from dcat:accessURL (may be a landing page or service URL) and dcat:mediaType / dcterms:format. schema.org Dataset.distribution points at DataDownload and states that different downloadable forms need not contain equivalent information. A dataset available only behind a web form still has a distribution whose access URL is that page.

questions.text: Is each distribution obtained by a direct download URL, a landing page, a mediated form, or an access service endpoint?
Do the distributions of this dataset serialize the same information, or do they differ by subset, language, profile, spatial resolution or schema?
What IANA media type and, if needed, additional format URI or label apply to each distribution?

data_elements.name: access_url
data_elements.description: URL through which the distribution is obtained

data_elements.name: download_url
data_elements.description: Direct file URL when one exists

data_elements.name: format
data_elements.description: Format or extent when not an IANA type

artifacts.name: Distribution descriptor
artifacts.description: Accessible representation of a dataset including URLs, media type and size.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the distribution identifier, which stays distinct from the dataset and data-service identifiers.

findings.name: Integrity and packaging
findings.description: DCAT 3 adds spdx:checksum / spdx:Checksum so a distribution can carry a digest and algorithm. DCAT-AP requires checksum algorithm and lowercase hexadecimal checksumValue when a checksum is present. DCAT also records compressFormat and packageFormat where a download is compressed or packaged. Byte size and checksum together support preservation manifests and bit-rot detection.

questions.text: What checksum algorithm and digest authenticate each downloadable distribution, and do they match bytes actually retrieved?
Is the download compressed or packaged, and which inner media type is the payload after unpacking?
What declared byte size applies, and is a size or digest mismatch treated as a failed distribution rather than as the same asset?

data_elements.name: package_format
data_elements.description: Packaging format such as ZIP or TAR

artifacts.name: Distribution checksum
artifacts.description: Algorithm and hex digest authenticating distribution bytes, plus compression and package formats.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the distribution identifier plus the checksum algorithm; the lowercase hex digest is an integrity value, not an identifier.

layers.name: Data service
layers.description: API endpoints that serve datasets, their declared API standards and their authentication requirements.

findings.name: Access service
findings.description: A dcat:DataService is a collection of operations accessible through an interface that provides access to datasets or processing functions. DCAT binds distributions via dcat:accessService and services via dcat:servesDataset, dcat:endpointURL and dcat:endpointDescription. dcterms:conformsTo on a service names the API standard, not the payload schema. DCAT-AP makes endpoint URL mandatory for data services. Service UI is out of scope.

questions.text: What endpoint URL and endpoint description document the operations of this data service, and which API standard does the service conform to?
Which datasets does this service serve, and which distributions, if any, expose the service as their accessService?
What authentication, authorisation or network restriction is required to call the endpoint, as distinct from the licence on the dataset?
Does dcterms:conformsTo on the service describe the API, while dataset or distribution conformsTo describes the payload schema or data specification?

data_elements.name: service_type
data_elements.description: Service type such as INSPIRE view or download

data_elements.name: auth_requirement
data_elements.description: Authentication or authorisation requirement declared for the endpoint

artifacts.name: Data service endpoint description
artifacts.description: Endpoint URL, API standard, endpoint description and datasets served.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the data-service identifier; the endpoint URL locates the service but does not replace its identifier.

layers.name: Rights and policy
layers.description: Licences, access-rights classes, machine-readable policies and applicable legislation bound to the dataset or its distributions.

findings.name: Licence and access rights
findings.description: DCAT records dcterms:license, dcterms:accessRights, dcterms:rights and odrl:hasPolicy on resources. Licences often attach to distributions; access rights often attach to the dataset. DataCite Rights is optional but important for reuse. DCAT-AP treats licence as a licence document and access rights as a rights statement, and adds applicable legislation. Open licences are explicit grants; absence of a licence is not a public-domain grant. Bilateral sharing agreements and API terms are contracts over the same asset, not additional datasets.

questions.text: Which licence applies to each distribution and to the dataset as a whole, and is any distribution under a different licence from its siblings?
What access-rights class applies (for example public, restricted, non-public), and which technical or legal conditions must a consumer satisfy before use?
Which legislation or regulation mandates publication, sharing or restriction of this dataset in the relevant jurisdiction?
If the dataset is not under a standard public licence, what data-sharing agreement or API access contract authorises use, and who are the parties?

data_elements.name: rights_statement
data_elements.description: Text or IRI of rights not covered by the licence

data_elements.name: applicable_legislation
data_elements.description: Legal resources mandating publication or reuse conditions

artifacts.name: Rights and licence binding
artifacts.description: Licence, access-rights classification, ODRL policy and applicable legislation attached to dataset or distribution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the node it attaches to, dataset or distribution, plus the licence document or policy IRI.

bundles.name: Series and lifecycle
bundles.description: Represent dataset series, version succession and resource status including publication, deprecation, withdrawal, embargo and invalidation.
bundles.rationale: Series membership, version succession and status are time-ordered relations between separately identified resources, and they must not be collapsed into distributions or dates.

layers.name: Dataset series
layers.description: Explicitly typed collections of separately published datasets and their first, previous and last navigation.

findings.name: Series membership
findings.description: DCAT 3 defines dcat:DatasetSeries as a dataset that represents a collection of datasets published separately but sharing characteristics. Navigation uses dcat:first, dcat:last and dcat:prev. DCAT-AP states that a Dataset with multiple Distributions is not thereby a Dataset Series; the DatasetSeries class must be used explicitly. ISO 19115 treats dataset series as a scope distinct from a single dataset.

questions.text: Is this asset an explicit DatasetSeries, a single Dataset with several distributions, or a mis-modelled series stored as one dataset with many files?
Which datasets are members of the series, and which are first, previous and last along the series dimension?
Which expected series slices are missing, delayed or superseded, and does the series remain current?

data_elements.name: series_dimension
data_elements.description: Dimension of variation such as time period or geography

artifacts.name: Dataset series membership
artifacts.description: Series identity, members and first/last/previous navigation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset series identifier; member datasets keep their own separate identifiers.

layers.name: Versioning
layers.description: Version tags, predecessor and successor links, current-version pointers and snapshot policy for changing datasets.

findings.name: Version succession
findings.description: DCAT 3 adds dcat:version, dcat:previousVersion, dcat:hasCurrentVersion, dcat:hasVersion, dcterms:replaces, adms:status and adms:versionNotes, replacing earlier dcterms hasVersion/isVersionOf URIs. DataCite Version is optional; relation types include HasVersion, IsVersionOf, IsNewVersionOf, IsPreviousVersionOf, Obsoletes and IsObsoletedBy. PROV models revisions with prov:wasRevisionOf and specializations with prov:specializationOf. A version identifier is not a date, though a version may correspond to a release event.

questions.text: What version tag identifies this dataset release, and which resource is the current version of the same work?
Which previous version does this resource succeed, which resources does it replace or obsolete, and which DataCite relationTypes apply if DOIs are used?
If the dataset is continuously updated, is this identifier bound to a snapshot, to a time-stamped query, or to a living work that is not citable as a fixed entity?

data_elements.name: datacite_relation
data_elements.description: DataCite relationType when a DOI graph is maintained

artifacts.name: Dataset version graph
artifacts.description: Version tag, predecessor and successor links, current-version pointer and notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the version tag bound to the resource identifier; version tags are not dates and retired identifiers are not recycled.

layers.name: Lifecycle status
layers.description: Status values and the event times of issuance, modification, availability, embargo, withdrawal and invalidation.

findings.name: Resource lifecycle status
findings.description: DCAT uses dcterms:issued, dcterms:modified and adms:status on catalogued resources. Typical ADMS statuses include under development, completed, deprecated and withdrawn. DataCite Date types include Available, Issued, Updated, Valid and Withdrawn. PROV records generation and invalidation times. Embargo is modelled as access restriction plus a future Available date, not as absence of identity. Withdrawal of a cited dataset should leave a tombstone at the persistent identifier rather than silent deletion.

questions.text: What status applies now (under development, completed, deprecated, withdrawn or a profile equivalent), and what event produced that status?
Is the dataset under embargo, until when does the embargo last, and which access-rights value applies during embargo versus after release?
If the dataset is withdrawn or invalidated, is a tombstone retained at the persistent identifier, are distributions disabled, and what successor if any is declared?
For the latest status change, what is the event time on the asset versus the observation or ingestion time on the catalogue record or harvest?

data_elements.name: status
data_elements.description: ADMS or profile status of the resource

data_elements.name: issued_at
data_elements.description: Formal issuance or publication event time

data_elements.name: modified_at
data_elements.description: Last modification event time of the asset

data_elements.name: available_at
data_elements.description: Date the resource became or will become available

data_elements.name: invalidated_at
data_elements.description: PROV invalidation time if the entity no longer exists as usable bytes

data_elements.name: embargo_until
data_elements.description: End of embargo if access is delayed

artifacts.name: Resource lifecycle status record
artifacts.description: Status, issuance, modification, availability, embargo and withdrawal or invalidation times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the resource identifier plus the status event time.

bundles.name: Coverage and extent
bundles.description: Record the temporal and spatial extent of the data content, update frequency and resolution, distinct from publication and catalogue timestamps.
bundles.rationale: Extent describes what the data is about, which is a different plane from when the description was issued or listed, and confusing the two breaks discovery.

layers.name: Temporal extent
layers.description: Time period covered by the data content, its resolution and the expected update frequency.

findings.name: Temporal coverage and frequency
findings.description: DCAT separates dcterms:issued and dcterms:modified (resource lifecycle) from dcterms:temporal coverage, dcat:temporalResolution and dcterms:accrualPeriodicity. Coverage is a period of time with start and end. DataCite Date with dateType Collected, Valid, Available or other values complements but does not replace coverage. ISO 19115 likewise separates reference dates from resource extent and maintenance frequency.

questions.text: What time period does the data content cover, and is the end open because the dataset is still accruing?
How frequently is the dataset expected to be updated, and what temporal resolution do the observations have?
If DataCite dates are recorded, which dates are Collected, Valid, Issued, Available, Updated or Withdrawn, and which of those are event times versus coverage?

data_elements.name: temporal_end
data_elements.description: End of content coverage, open if ongoing

data_elements.name: temporal_resolution
data_elements.description: Minimum spacing of items as xsd:duration

artifacts.name: Temporal extent record
artifacts.description: Content time period, resolution, accrual periodicity and collected or valid dates.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset identifier; coverage periods are content properties and are never used as identifiers.

layers.name: Spatial extent
layers.description: Places, geometries and spatial resolution describing where the data content applies.

findings.name: Spatial coverage and resolution
findings.description: DCAT records dcterms:spatial coverage and dcat:spatialResolutionInMeters. DataCite GeoLocation is recommended and supports place names, bounding boxes and polygons. ISO 19115 identification and extent packages are the geospatial community's richer model, including coordinate reference systems that DCAT does not itself define. Location of the data content is not the same as PROV location of an activity or file path.

questions.text: What named places, gazetteer IRIs or geometries describe the spatial coverage of the data content?
What spatial resolution in metres, equivalent scale, or other resolution measure applies, if any?
In which coordinate reference system are coverage geometries expressed, and is that CRS recorded here or only in a geospatial sibling profile?

data_elements.name: spatial_coverage
data_elements.description: Named place, geometry or gazetteer IRI

data_elements.name: coordinate_reference_system
data_elements.description: CRS of geometries when ISO or GeoSPARQL geometry is used

artifacts.name: Spatial extent record
artifacts.description: Coverage location or geometry, resolution and CRS when known.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset identifier; coverage geometries are content properties and are never used as identifiers.

bundles.name: Structure, lineage and quality
bundles.description: Attach declared schema or standard conformance, generation and derivation pointers, and quality evidence without duplicating sibling schema, lineage and quality models.
bundles.rationale: Structure, provenance and quality each have their own sibling model; this bundle keeps only the dataset-level pointers needed to navigate to them.

layers.name: Schema conformance
layers.description: Declared conformance of the dataset, distribution or service to standards, schemas and application profiles.

findings.name: Declared schema and standard conformance
findings.description: DCAT uses dcterms:conformsTo for a standard, schema or application profile the resource follows. That property is a pointer: field-level contracts live in WM-DAT-004. DCAT-AP distinguishes service API conformance from dataset payload conformance. Adopting a new schema version is a dataset lifecycle event, not a silent overwrite. This model does not store the schema document itself.

questions.text: Which schema, data contract, application profile or content standard does this dataset or distribution declare conformance to, and which sibling schema record in WM-DAT-004 holds the structure?
When did this dataset adopt the current schema version, and which previous schema version did it leave?
What validation evidence exists for the declared conformance, and is that evidence a SHACL or schema-validation artifact in WM-DAT-004 rather than a catalogue field?

data_elements.name: conforms_to
data_elements.description: IRIs of standards, schemas or profiles

data_elements.name: schema_version
data_elements.description: Declared version of the schema or contract

data_elements.name: schema_model_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to WM-DAT-004 schema or data-contract instance

artifacts.name: Conformance declaration
artifacts.description: Pointers to schemas, standards or profiles the dataset or distribution claims to follow.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the conformance target, dataset, distribution or service, plus the standard or profile IRI and declared schema version.

layers.name: Lineage pointer
layers.description: Dataset-level generation, derivation and attribution pointers into the lineage sibling model.

findings.name: Generation and derivation
findings.description: DCAT reuses prov:wasGeneratedBy on datasets. PROV-O provides wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, used, wasInvalidatedBy and qualified influence classes for chains of entities, activities and agents. ISO 19115 resource lineage (LI_Lineage) records sources and processes; some profiles make lineage mandatory. Detailed activity graphs belong in WM-DAT-006; this finding only requires dataset-level pointers sufficient to navigate to that sibling.

questions.text: From which source datasets or entities was this dataset derived, and which activity generated it?
Is there a primary source, revision, quotation or other PROV-qualified derivation that must be distinguished from a generic derivedFrom link?
Is a lineage statement or ISO LI_Lineage record present, mandatory under the applicable profile, and complete enough to replay the derivation in WM-DAT-006?

artifacts.name: Lineage pointer
artifacts.description: Dataset-level generation, derivation and attribution pointers into the lineage sibling model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the generated dataset identifier plus the generating activity reference held in the lineage sibling model.

layers.name: Quality pointer
layers.description: DQV measurements, certificates and fitness judgements attached to the catalogued asset as composed evidence.

findings.name: Quality measurements and fitness
findings.description: DQV extends DCAT so a dataset or distribution can have quality measurements, annotations, certificates, policies and conformance to standards. A measurement is computedOn the dataset, isMeasurementOf a metric, sits in a dimension and category, and has a value and optional unit. DQV states that quality is fitness for purpose in the eye of the beholder; publishers are not the only assessors. ISO 19157 holds geospatial data-quality measures that ISO 19115-1 no longer contains. Detailed metric definitions and assessment campaigns belong in WM-DAT-007.

questions.text: Which quality metrics, dimensions and values have been computed on this dataset or distribution, when, and by whom?
For which stated purposes has fitness been asserted or certified, and is that judgement from the publisher, a third-party certificate, or user feedback?
If multiple agents published conflicting quality statements, which statements are in force for catalogue display versus steward dashboards?

artifacts.name: Quality evidence attachment
artifacts.description: Pointers to DQV measurements, certificates or feedback held in the quality sibling model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the measured resource plus the metric and the assessment event time, since a DQV measurement is computed on a specific node.

bundles.name: Stewardship and governance
bundles.description: Identify accountable agents, legal and security constraints, and persistence, withdrawal and erasure rules for the catalogued asset.
bundles.rationale: Accountability, constraint and retention decisions are made by named agents over the whole asset, and they outlive any single distribution or version.

layers.name: Agent roles
layers.description: Holder, publisher, creators, contributors, contact points and funders, with attribution kept distinct from ownership.

findings.name: Holder, publisher and attribution
findings.description: DCAT attributes dcterms:publisher, dcterms:creator, dcat:contactPoint and prov:qualifiedAttribution with roles. DataCite distinguishes mandatory Creator and Publisher from recommended Contributor with contributorType. DCAT-AP requires a named publisher on the catalogue and treats Agent as any entity acting on catalogues and catalogued resources. The data holder is accountable for content and service levels; a catalogue operator lists the asset but does not become the holder by harvesting it. FundingReference is optional DataCite metadata, not ownership.

questions.text: Who is the data holder accountable for content and service levels, and is that party the same as the catalogue publisher?
Who are the creators and contributors, with which identifiers and DataCite contributor types or PROV roles?
What contact point receives comments, quality feedback and access requests for this dataset?
Which funders or awards supported creation of the dataset, and do any of those awards impose deposit, embargo or licence obligations without transferring holdership?

data_elements.name: creators
data_elements.description: Creators with identifiers such as ORCID or ROR

data_elements.name: contact_point
data_elements.description: Contact for comments and access requests

artifacts.name: Agent attribution record
artifacts.description: Holder, publisher, creators, contributors, contact point and qualified roles.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset identifier plus agent identifiers such as ORCID or ROR and the qualified role.

layers.name: Constraints and retention
layers.description: Legal, security and privacy constraints on the asset and its metadata, and the persistence, withdrawal and erasure policy applied to it.

findings.name: Legal, security and privacy constraints
findings.description: ISO 19115 constraint information covers legal and security constraints on the resource and on its metadata. DCAT carries accessRights, rights and ODRL policies but does not define a security-classification code list. Personal data, statistical disclosure control and export-control restrictions are constraints on the catalogued asset; they are not a reason to omit the asset from an internal register. Catalogue metadata may be public while distributions remain restricted.

questions.text: What legal constraints and security classification apply to the dataset bytes versus to the catalogue metadata?
Does the dataset contain personal or otherwise disclosive data, and which processing lawful basis or statistical disclosure rule governs access?
What use limitations, purpose restrictions or prohibited uses are declared, beyond the licence document?

data_elements.name: metadata_constraints
data_elements.description: Constraints that apply to metadata rather than to data bytes

artifacts.name: Resource constraint set
artifacts.description: Legal, security, privacy and metadata-use constraints on the catalogued asset.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the constrained resource and by whether the constraint applies to data bytes or to metadata.

findings.name: Persistence, withdrawal and erasure
findings.description: Cited datasets should remain resolvable. DataCite supports a Withdrawn date type while keeping the DOI. PROV models invalidation when an entity is no longer usable. DCAT deprecated and withdrawn statuses cover holder-initiated removal from service. Retention schedules and legal erasure obligations can conflict with citation persistence; the operational pattern is tombstone plus suppressed distributions, not identifier reuse. This finding records the dataset-level policy; it does not encode a full records-management model.

questions.text: After withdrawal or legal erasure, does the persistent identifier still resolve to a tombstone, and are prior checksums retained as evidence of what was removed?
Must distribution bytes be erased, encrypted-beyond-use, or only delisted, and under which request or schedule?
Is reuse of the retired dataset identifier forbidden, and which successor identifier should consumers follow?

data_elements.name: persist_pid
data_elements.description: Whether the identifier remains resolvable after withdrawal

data_elements.name: tombstone_policy
data_elements.description: Tombstone behaviour at the PID and catalogue

data_elements.name: erasure_request_ref
data_elements.description: Legal erasure or take-down request if any

data_elements.name: retention_end
data_elements.description: Scheduled end of retention if any

artifacts.name: Dataset retention and withdrawal policy binding
artifacts.description: Retention schedule, tombstone rules, byte-erasure flags and take-down references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the dataset persistent identifier plus the retention schedule; retired identifiers are not reused.

functions.name: Register dataset in a catalogue
functions.description: Create a catalogued resource and optional catalogue record with identity, publisher, title and listing timestamps.
preconditions: dataset identifier is unique in the catalogue of record
effects: listing event time recorded on the record
observation time of registration recorded if distinct

functions.name: Publish distribution
functions.description: Add an accessible representation with access or download URL, media type, optional checksum and licence.
preconditions: URL is reachable under declared access rights
effects: dataset becomes available through at least one distribution

functions.name: Bind data service
functions.description: Attach a data service endpoint that serves the dataset and optionally backs a distribution.
preconditions: service versus payload conformance targets are distinct

functions.name: Version dataset
functions.description: Mint a new dataset version, link previous and current versions, and record version notes without recycling identifiers.
preconditions: new identifier is not a date and is not reused

functions.name: Attach dataset to series
functions.description: Add a separately published dataset to an explicit DatasetSeries and update first, previous and last navigation.
preconditions: member is not being faked as an extra distribution of another member

functions.name: Harvest catalogue
functions.description: Import DCAT-shaped metadata from a source catalogue, preserving source records and distinguishing harvest observation time from source event time.
outputs: local catalogue records with source metadata links
preconditions: receiver can process all DCAT-AP classes and controlled vocabularies in scope
effects: harvested copies linked to source records
ingestion time stored separately from issued and listing times

functions.name: Attach quality assessment
functions.description: Attach DQV measurements, certificates or feedback computed on the dataset or distribution, storing detailed results in WM-DAT-007.

functions.name: Record generation or derivation
functions.description: Point the dataset at generating activities and source entities, composing WM-DAT-006 for the full graph.
preconditions: activity times use RFC 3339 with seconds and offset

functions.name: Deprecate or withdraw dataset
functions.description: Mark a dataset deprecated or withdrawn, disable or erase distributions per policy, and keep a tombstone at the persistent identifier.
preconditions: consumers of citations still resolve the PID
effects: distributions suppressed or erased according to retention policy

functions.name: Cite dataset
functions.description: Build a citation from mandatory DataCite-style properties and the chosen persistent identifier.
preconditions: mandatory citation properties present or replaced with DataCite unknown codes
effects: isReferencedBy relations may be added on the dataset

functions.name: Validate catalogue profile
functions.description: Check a catalogue or dataset description against DCAT and a chosen application profile, including SHACL where DCAT-AP provides it.
effects: validation status recorded; nonconformance does not itself change dataset status

functions.name: Apply access policy
functions.description: Grant or deny access to distributions or services according to licence, access rights, ODRL policy and exceptions, with audit.
preconditions: holder or delegated access authority is known
effects: access granted, denied or exception recorded

composition.purpose: Dataset or distribution dcterms:conformsTo a schema, data contract or standard whose structure is governed in the schema model. Semantic contract versus catalogue asset; field-level structure must not be duplicated here.
Dataset includes lineage context via prov:wasGeneratedBy, prov:wasDerivedFrom and ISO lineage pointers. Provenance pattern; full activity graphs stay in the lineage model.
Dataset includes quality assessments via DQV measurements, certificates and feedback. Quality evidence attaches to the catalogued asset; metric definitions and campaigns stay in the quality model.
Inbound: the data product catalog entry in WM-DAT-008 references datasets as the bytes or collections offered. Offering versus bytes; commercial packaging is not a dataset.
Inbound: a training run in WM-AI-006 references datasets used as training, validation or evaluation material. Training provenance; run configuration is not dataset catalogue metadata.
Inbound production link: a research study in WM-ACT-036 produces datasets as research outputs that are then catalogued. Research output; study protocol remains in the activity model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension package MUST name the data holder accountable for dataset content, declared quality, licences and service levels, and MUST keep that party distinct from the catalogue operator.
The adopting Dimension package MUST declare its catalogue of record and the identifier scheme used before minting dataset, distribution, data-service or catalogue-record identifiers.
The adopting Dimension package MUST publish AGENTS.md with Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update operation.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Dataset, distribution, data service, catalogue and catalogue-record IRIs are minted in the owner Dimension's own namespace and kept dereferenceable and pairwise distinct; blank nodes are discouraged for main DCAT classes because they cannot be reused as link targets, and retired identifiers are never re-minted in the same namespace.
registry_links: Vercy world-model registry entry WM-DAT-001 (this model) with its sibling entries WM-DAT-004, WM-DAT-006, WM-DAT-007 and WM-DAT-008.
Controlled-vocabulary registries relied on by the profiles cited here: EU NAL data themes, frequency, licence and access-right vocabularies for DCAT-AP exchange.
Identifier and format registries: DataCite DOI registration, IANA media types and SPDX checksum algorithms.

canonicalization_rules: Time values are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, with event time stored separately from observation or ingestion time.
Checksum values are canonicalized to lowercase hexadecimal and always carry an explicit algorithm.
Identifiers are canonicalized to the governed IRI or DOI form recorded in the identity priority; a date is never canonicalized into an identifier position.
patch_rules: A patch to descriptive metadata updates dcterms:modified on the asset and the catalogue-record modification date separately; harvested copies preserve source-record identity.

A patch never re-points or recycles a retired identifier; substantive change mints a new version linked with previousVersion, hasCurrentVersion and, where DOIs are used, the matching DataCite relationType.
Withdrawal is patched as status plus withdrawal or invalidation time and a tombstone, never as deletion of the record.
compatibility_rules: Adopting a new schema or profile version is recorded as a lifecycle event with the adoption time and the previous version, not as a silent overwrite.
Consumers resolve across versions through dcat:hasCurrentVersion and dcat:previousVersion; DCAT 2 dcterms hasVersion/isVersionOf usage is migrated to the DCAT 3 properties that DCAT-AP 3.0 documents.
Profile-level validation failure is recorded as a conformance report and does not by itself change dataset status.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record event time (issued, modified, generated, available, withdrawn, invalidated, quality-assessed) separately from observation or ingestion time (catalogue-record listing, record modified, harvest, metadata ingest) when those differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Sequential numbers such as catalogue accession numbers are not dataset identity; where a catalogue issues them they are recorded as alternate identifiers scoped to the issuing catalogue, are never used as the master identifier, and are never reissued after withdrawal.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Dataset, distribution, data-service, catalogue and catalogue-record identifiers MUST be distinct and MUST NOT be dates. Downloadable distributions SHOULD carry an spdx:Checksum with algorithm and lowercase hex digest. A catalogue record foaf:primaryTopic identifies exactly one catalogued resource. Silent deletion of a cited dataset is forbidden; withdrawal uses status plus tombstone at the persistent identifier. Blank nodes for main DCAT classes are discouraged because they cannot be reused as link targets.

policies: The data holder is accountable for content and service levels; catalogue operators list and harvest but do not become holders by copying metadata.
Absence of a licence is not a grant; open reuse requires an explicit licence or rights statement on the dataset or distribution.
Multiple distributions of one dataset are not automatically a dataset series; DatasetSeries must be typed explicitly.
Quality statements are assessments by named agents, not intrinsic properties of bytes; conflicting assessments may coexist and are composed from WM-DAT-007.
Persistent identifiers of cited datasets are not recycled; legal erasure suppresses bytes and may tombstone metadata but does not mint the same identifier for a new work.
Schema, lineage and quality internals are referenced or composed from sibling models rather than copied.
Event time and catalogue observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever they differ.
Access defaults to the declared accessRights; public licences are explicit exceptions to a deny-for-non-public default in internal registers.

read: Resolve master-system identifier, IRI or DOI to the catalogued resource.
Discover datasets by theme, type, coverage, publisher and quality pointers.
Retrieve distribution descriptors, checksums and access or download URLs.
Read catalogue records, harvest provenance and version or series navigation.
Export a profile-shaped harvest feed without exposing holder-only lineage or restricted quality detail.
create: Register a dataset in a catalogue of record with publisher, title and unique identifiers.
Mint or bind a DOI or other governed PID when the dataset is a citable output.
Add distributions, data services, series membership and catalogue records.
Attach lineage and quality pointers to sibling model instances.
Record licences, access rights and constraint sets at create time.
update: Revise descriptive metadata, themes, coverage and contact points.
Add versions, replace links and version notes without identifier reuse.
Change ADMS or profile status, embargo windows and available dates.
Add or rotate distributions and checksums; bind additional services.
Update harvest copies while preserving source-record identity and event versus ingestion times.
delete: Deprecate a dataset still resolvable but discouraged.
Withdraw a dataset from service with tombstone at the persistent identifier.
Erase or delist distribution bytes when retention, take-down or legal erasure requires it.
Remove a catalogue record from a harvested catalogue without deleting the holder asset.
Never recycle identifiers or silently delete cited assets.

roles.name: Data holder
responsibilities: Accountable for dataset content, declared quality, licences and service levels.
Assigns or binds the authoritative master-system identifier.
Authorises publication, restriction, deprecation, withdrawal and erasure.

roles.name: Publisher
responsibilities: Makes the dataset available in a catalogue.
May be the holder or an agent acting for the holder.
Supplies citation metadata required by the chosen identifier system.

roles.name: Catalogue operator
responsibilities: Operates the register, harvest and discovery services.
Maintains catalogue records distinct from dataset identity.
Does not become holder by listing or harvesting.

roles.name: Data steward
responsibilities: Keeps classification, coverage, schema pointers, lineage pointers and lifecycle status current.
Coordinates version and series navigation.
Raises integrity failures such as checksum mismatch.

roles.name: Quality assessor
responsibilities: Computes or certifies DQV measurements and fitness judgements.
May be the holder, an aggregator, a user or a certification body.
Publishes assessments into WM-DAT-007 and attaches them here.

roles.name: Access authority
responsibilities: Evaluates licence, accessRights, ODRL policy and legal exceptions.
Grants or denies service and download access with audit.
Handles embargo release and take-down execution.

roles.name: Harvester
responsibilities: Ingests foreign catalogues under a declared profile.
Preserves source records and timestamps.
Must not collapse harvested copies into a false catalogue of record.

roles.name: Consumer
responsibilities: Discovers, cites and reuses datasets under declared rights.
May submit user quality feedback.
Must treat non-equivalent distributions as distinct representations.

access.default_rule: Deny distribution and service access unless the dataset or distribution declares a public licence or an equivalent public accessRights value; catalogue discovery metadata may still be readable according to metadata constraints.
exceptions: Explicit public licence or public accessRights on the dataset or distribution.
Bilateral data-sharing agreement or API access contract naming the requesting agent and purpose.
Embargo expiry that flips accessRights from restricted to public at the available date.
Statutory open-data mandates recorded as applicable legislation.
Legal erasure, court order or security classification that suppresses even metadata that would otherwise be public.
audit_requirements: Log identifier minting, status changes, harvest ingest, access decisions, checksum verification failures, withdrawal and erasure with event time and observation time.
Retain audit records of access grants and denials at artifact scope for restricted distributions.
Record the agent, role and policy version used for each exception.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update.
Resolve Specification URL to this model's catalogue-asset semantics; treat Storage type URL and Interface URL as projections, not as alternative meanings.
Follow Processes URL for register, publish, harvest, version, withdraw and access-grant procedures.
Load sibling schema, lineage and quality models only through the composition links, not by inferring them from storage documents.

coverage.claim: This meta-model covers catalogued-dataset semantics needed to identify, describe, list, distribute, version, constrain and retire datasets, aligned to W3C DCAT 3, SEMIC DCAT-AP 3.0, DataCite Metadata Schema 4.7, W3C DQV, W3C PROV-O and ISO 19115-1 discovery packages. It is not a claim of universal completeness, of byte-level data modelling, or of conformance of any particular catalogue.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifiers, IRIs, DataCite DOI, alternate identifiers, and distinct IDs for dataset, distribution, service and catalogue record.
Issued, modified, ADMS status, embargo, deprecation, withdrawal, PROV invalidation, series slices and version succession.
Catalogue membership, series navigation, version graph, servesDataset, accessService, derivedFrom, product and training inbound references.
Content coverage, resolution, accrual periodicity, DataCite date types, and event time versus catalogue observation or ingestion time.
Dataset-level PROV generation and derivation pointers composed with WM-DAT-006; harvest source records.
Holder versus publisher versus catalogue operator; creators, contributors, contact points and funding as attribution not ownership.
Declared dcterms:conformsTo and profile validation as pointers to WM-DAT-004 and DCAT-AP SHACL; checksum verification of distributions.
downloadURL versus accessURL versus data service; licence, accessRights, ODRL, auth requirements and exceptions.
Tombstone-on-withdraw, forbidden identifier reuse, byte erasure versus delist, conflict with citation persistence recorded as a policy tension.
DCAT 3 core, DCAT-AP 3.0 profiles, DataCite citation, schema.org Dataset equivalent class, ISO 19115-1 alignment without claimed conformance.
dcat class, dcterms:type, themes, DataCite resourceTypeGeneral and ISO scope codes.
DQV measurements, certificates and fitness attached as composed evidence, not as an intrinsic score.
Coverage, bounding box, resolution; CRS treated as geospatial-profile detail.

known_omissions: ISO 19115-1 full element dictionaries and ISO 19157 quality measures were not read from the ISO paywalled texts; geospatial constraint and lineage packages are aligned from public summaries and ICSM guidance.

FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data 2016) and GDPR Article 17 erasure were not retrieved as live primary pages in this run; persistence versus erasure is modelled from DataCite withdrawal, DCAT status and PROV invalidation only.
DDI Codebook, SDMX dataflow, Frictionless Data Package, STAC, Croissant ML metadata and Datasheets for Datasets are emerging or domain profiles not modelled as core.
OAIS SIP/AIP/DIP packaging, CKAN extras and physical-media distributions are not modelled.
Agent and organisation master data, identifier-scheme registries and official-statistics methodology are sibling concerns without model IDs in the supplied registry extract.
Continuously updated databases versus snapshot datasets are only covered through the dynamic-dataset versioning question.
Confidential-computing clean rooms and dataset pricing belong elsewhere.
conflicts: DCAT Dataset (conceptual collection with distributions and services) versus ISO 19115 dataset (geographic resource with identification, constraint, lineage, extent and, historically, quality packages now in ISO 19157).
DCAT-AP 3.0: a Dataset with multiple Distributions is not a DatasetSeries unless the DatasetSeries class is used explicitly; some publishers still model series as many files on one dataset.
DataCite Identifier in its registry is a DOI; DCAT allows any dcterms:identifier. Citation systems and catalogues therefore disagree on which identifier is mandatory.
schema.org Dataset is equivalentClass dcat:Dataset, but schema.org explicitly allows non-equivalent DataDownload variants; some harvest pipelines assume byte-equivalent mirrors.
DQV treats quality as fitness judged by many agents; ISO 19157 and many statistical offices treat quality as measured characteristics of the data.
DataCite PublicationYear (gYear, mandatory) versus dcterms:issued (full date, optional in DCAT).
DCAT 3 replaced dcterms hasVersion/isVersionOf mappings used in DCAT 2; DCAT-AP 3.0 documents that URI change.
Catalogue-record identifier versus dataset identifier versus DOI; harvesters that mint a new ID per copy create false duplicates.
Legal erasure and security take-down versus citation persistence and FAIR-style findability; operational resolution is tombstone plus suppressed bytes, not a single global rule.
Data product (WM-DAT-008 offering) versus dataset (this model); treating a SKU as a dataset or a dataset as a product mixes planes.
regional_assumptions: European exchanges using DCAT-AP 3.0 are assumed to require NAL data-theme for dcat:theme and the DCAT-AP controlled vocabularies for frequency, licences and access rights.
United States federal open-data catalogues often follow DCAT-US three-tier Catalog/Dataset/Distribution practice; DatasetSeries adoption may lag DCAT 3.
Research repositories that mint DataCite DOIs treat Creator, Title, Publisher, PublicationYear and ResourceType as mandatory regardless of DCAT optionality.
Geospatial agencies using ISO 19115-1/19157 and INSPIRE remain more constraint- and lineage-heavy than generic open-data portals.
Personal-data and statistical-disclosure rules are jurisdiction-specific; this model records flags and policies but does not encode a single privacy statute.
adversarial_checks: Using a publication date or coverage end date as the dataset identifier, violating identity priority and the date-is-not-an-identifier rule.
Treating harvested catalogue-record IDs as dataset IDs, producing duplicate assets that break PID resolution.
Encoding a series as many distributions of one dataset, then losing slice-level issued dates and missing-slice semantics.
Assuming all distributions are information-equivalent and overwriting a subset GeoJSON with a full CSV as if they were the same bytes.
Storing a landing-page URL as downloadURL, causing automated fetchers to retrieve HTML and fail checksums.
Publishing quality scores without metric, dimension, assessor and assessment event time, which DQV does not support.
Silently deleting a cited dataset instead of withdrawing with a tombstone, breaking DataCite and catalogue harvests.
Copying WM-DAT-004 field maps, WM-DAT-006 graphs or WM-DAT-007 metric catalogues into this model and claiming a single record is the contract.
Claiming DCAT-AP or ISO 19115 conformance because properties are present, without profile SHACL or ISO core discovery obligation checks.
Collapsing holder, publisher and catalogue operator so a harvester appears to own the data.
